main_results.chord_almost_in_the_kernel: norm_comp_apply_sub_le_of_approximatesLinearOn: for two points of one fibre the chord satisfies a bound by ||P|| times epsilon times the chord length; this is the ONLY place the fibre hypothesis is used and the exact point where the situation differs from the vanishing-derivative case, because the chord is NOT in the kernel
main_results.R4: exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_ker_bound: the projected map is Lipschitz with constant c times epsilon on every fibre, with c = ||Q|| (1 + ||A|| C ||P||) depending only on the linear data and NEVER on epsilon, on f, on S or on the fibre
main_results.why_the_constant_matters: the epsilon to zero limit of the Eilenberg argument uses a different approximating partition at every scale, so a constant growing with the partition would be useless; the independence is visible in the statement shape, exists c for all epsilon
main_results.stratum_corollary: exists_lipschitzOnWith_fibre: what R2, R3 and R4 combine to on a rank stratum. A COROLLARY OF THREE PROVED OBLIGATIONS, NOT A NEW ONE, and in particular NOT R7: no measure, Hausdorff dimension, slice or approximating partition appears

hypothesis_analysis.rank_zero_end: zero_model_recovers_vanishing_derivative: with A = 0 both hypotheses hold with C = 0, the constant collapses to ||Q||, and R4 returns exactly the proved vanishing-derivative situation, ADDING NOTHING on the r = 0 layer
